subject: clockworkDog
pitch: A wind-up clockwork terrier made of polished brass and copper. Riveted body plates, visible gears turning in its chest, a big winding key on its back, springy jointed legs, floppy leather ears, glass-lens eyes with a green tint, a tail made of a coiled spring, and a little red collar with a brass tag.
reasoning:
I'm planning a terrier-sized dog model facing forward, working out proportions and a skeleton hierarchy with pelvis root, spine-to-head chain, four-legged limb joints down to paws, and a tail chain.

Now I'm sketching out the construction details: leg placements with hip/knee/paw joints, a helper function to build cylinder limb segments aimed between two points, springy coiled shins using torus rings, and a material palette of brass, copper, dark bronze, red, and green glass tones, plus plans for riveted body plates.

For the torso I'm defining a copper box frame with brass side panels and rivets, a front glass window exposing gear mechanisms, and a reusable gear-building function with teeth arranged radially around a hinge joint so they can later be animated turning.

For the head I'm adding a copper box with a brass upper jaw/snout and a separate lower jaw piece.

Now I'm designing the winding key on the back with a hinged stem and butterfly-style handle using torus loops lying flat in the xy plane, then starting on the tail as a coiled spring section at the rear.

Building the chain path...

Now I'm mapping out the spine joints from pelvis through spine1, chest, neck, up to the head position.

Adding leg joint definitions...

Still placing leg segments and joints...

Adding more gear details...

Adding dark pupils and planning the ear geometry now, with joints hanging from the head and angled plate segments forming each floppy ear shape.

Now I'm setting up the leather color with brass rivets at the ear base, checking torso clearance above the floor, and placing a neck cylinder with a red collar torus and a small tag disc.

I'm adding a small ring for the tag and a brass buckle box at the collar, deciding to keep the palette simple. Then I'm writing a helper function that builds cylindrical body segments between two 3D points, computing their midpoint, length, and orientation for consistent limb geometry.

Now I'm defining additional helpers: a box-building function for flat plates, a rivet function using small spheres with a light brass color, and setting up how plates like ears get oriented between two points along a bone. I'm also starting a loop over left/right leg sides to generate the hip and knee segments symmetrically.

For the legs, I'm planning to use a chain helper that takes a polyline of four points (hip, knee, ankle, paw) with matching names, letting joint orientation get computed automatically along the path. I'm sketching similar chain logic for the spine, running from pelvis through to the head, though I need to make sure the root joint exists before the chain can attach to it.

Mapping out the neck chain from chest to head with intermediate points, then placing jaw, ears, legs, and tail each parented to the appropriate body part, and confirming the chest joint's tip name serves as the reference for downstream chains.

Now I'm laying out the tail with tapering rings and a brass ball end, and placing the key mechanism's stem, hub, and winding loops at the top of the body.
